en: Oṃ, homage to the stainless one. Oṃ, homage to the consciousness that contains fire within. Oṃ, homage to the leader. Oṃ, homage to the unborn. Oṃ, homage to the one possessing a wondrous form. Oṃ, homage to the supreme overseer. Oṃ, homage to the one worshipped by many. Oṃ, homage to the one whose form is unmanifest. Oṃ, homage to the imperishable. Oṃ, homage to the imperishable. Oṃ, homage to the one who is relied upon. Oṃ, homage to the bestower of Indra’s glory. Oṃ, homage to the bearer of the sugarcane bow. Oṃ, homage to the one with a blue lotus in hand. Oṃ, homage to the one with a single tusk.

Oṃ, salutations to the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age. Oṃ, salutations to the beloved. Oṃ, salutations to the lover. Oṃ, salutations to Time. Oṃ, salutations to the shatterer of the mountain of the lineage. Oṃ, salutations to the skillful one. Oṃ, salutations to the giver of the bliss of absolute liberation. Oṃ, salutations to the elephant-faced one. Oṃ, salutations to the Lord of the Gaṇas. Oṃ, salutations to the refuge. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has transcended the qualities. Oṃ, salutations to the son of Gaurī. Oṃ, salutations to the Lord of the planets. Oṃ, salutations to the wielder of the discus. Oṃ, salutations to the fierce one. Oṃ, salutations to the clever one.

Oṃ, salutation to the four-armed one. Oṃ, salutation to the one of four forms. Oṃ, salutation to the crest-jewel of the moon. Oṃ, salutation to the one with matted hair. Oṃ, salutation to the contented one. Oṃ, salutation to the one endowed with compassion. Oṃ, salutation to the skillful one. Oṃ, salutation to the self-controlled one. Oṃ, salutation to the one who loves *dūrvā* grass and *bilva* leaves. Oṃ, salutation to the divine one. Oṃ, salutation to the one dear to the twice-born. Oṃ, salutation to the son of Dvimātṛ. Oṃ, salutation to the steadfast one. Oṃ, salutation to the one who wears the sacred thread made of the king of serpents. Oṃ, salutation to the stainless one.

Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme. Oṃ, salutation to the remover of sins. Oṃ, salutation to the wielder of the noose and the goad. Oṃ, salutation to the pure one. Oṃ, salutation to the one who causes fear to the arrogant Daityas. Oṃ, salutation to the serene-souled one. Oṃ, salutation to the one intent upon the citron fruit. Oṃ, salutation to the beloved of wisdom. Oṃ, salutation to the celibate student. Oṃ, salutation to the one free from hatred toward Brahman. Oṃ, salutation to the supreme knower of Brahman. Oṃ, salutation to the giver of the desires of devotees.

Oṃ, salutations to the destroyer of obstacles for devotees. Oṃ, salutations to the one who loves devotion. Oṃ, salutations to the wielder of Māyā. Oṃ, salutations to the one praised by sages. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose vehicle is a mouse. Oṃ, salutations to the one worshipped by Ramā. Oṃ, salutations to the long-bellied one. Oṃ, salutations to the giver of boons. Oṃ, salutations to the Lord of Speech. Oṃ, salutations to the bestower of eloquence. Oṃ, salutations to the King of Obstacles. Oṃ, salutations to the Creator. Oṃ, salutations to Vināyaka. Oṃ, salutations to the Sovereign Lord of the universe. Oṃ, salutations to the one free from fear.

Oṃ, salutation to the one endowed with power (Śakti). Oṃ, salutation to the peaceful one (Śānta). Oṃ, salutation to the eternal one (Śāśvata). Oṃ, salutation to the auspicious one (Śiva). Oṃ, salutation to the pure one (Śuddha). Oṃ, salutation to the one with ears like winnowing baskets (Śūrpakarṇa). Oṃ, salutation to the one whose mind is eager for the sport of dalliance on the lap of the daughter of the Lord of Mountains (Pārvatī). Oṃ, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha. Oṃ, salutation to the one who bestows prosperity (Śrīkara). Oṃ, salutation to the giver of fortune (Śrīda). Oṃ, salutation to the abode of Śrī. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss (Saccidānanda-vigraha). Oṃ, salutation to the support of the entire universe (Samastajagadādhāra).

Oṃ, homage to the one who is composed in meditative absorption. Oṃ, homage to the father of all. Oṃ, homage to the one dear to Sarvarī. Oṃ, homage to the bestower of all accomplishments. Oṃ, homage to the one who bestows all accomplishments. Oṃ, homage to the one whose self is everything. Oṃ, homage to the one who loves the sound of the Sāman chants. Oṃ, homage to the one whose lotus feet are worshipped by the Siddhas. Oṃ, homage to the giver of accomplishment. Oṃ, homage to the creator of the universe. Oṃ, homage to the one whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and fire. Oṃ, homage to the gentle one. Oṃ, homage to the elder brother of Skanda.

Oṃ, salutation to the one delighted by praise. Oṃ, salutation to the thick-necked one. Oṃ, salutation to the thick-snouted one. Oṃ, salutation to the self-creator. Oṃ, salutation to the self-perfected one. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose form has surpassed the God of Love with the essence of his own exquisite beauty. Oṃ, salutation to Hari. Oṃ, salutation to the joyful one. Oṃ, salutation to the wise one. Thus ends the *Śrī Vināyaka Aṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī* (The Hundred and Eight Names of Vināyaka).
